_note:
This is the game's DEFAULT style — the CAMERA, the RENDERING and the PALETTE, and nothing else. It is prepended to every art prompt for this game: room passes (.github/art/room.py), character rows (.github/art/generate_row.py) and the 'Generate game asset' Action all read it.

IT DOES NOT DESCRIBE THE ROOM PIPELINE, AND MUST NOT. That lives in docs/ROOM_ART_STANDARD.md and in the pass prompts under .github/art/room_prompts/, which are the single copy of the recipe. This file used to restate it — back when a room was TWO layers — and it drifted: long after the standard became THREE passes, this file was still telling the generator that a floor plate is 'a complete floor and its surrounding architecture', and that any door 'MUST be on the back-right wall'. Because styled() puts this text IN FRONT of the pass prompt, the stale copy won: the lounge's pass-2 plate came back as planks in a painted brown vignette instead of on flat white, which keys to nothing and makes the whole frame walkable. If a rule about how rooms are built belongs anywhere, it belongs in the pass prompt — point at it from here, never copy it.

HISTORY of the style itself, in one day: (1) close-up cinematic-portrait camera used for rooms by mistake — looked like a photo backdrop with cutouts standing in front; (2) fixed the camera but kept painterly/vignette rendering — still murky, user said 'think Stardew Valley'; (3) went fully flat cel-shaded Stardew — user said that 'doesn't fit the bill' and pointed back at the inspiration images and the already-generated portraits as the real target: richly saturated, moody, warm-vs-cool lit, textured.
camera:
Top-down RPG interior room view: a clean, gently-angled overhead perspective, orthogonal walls, a clearly readable floor plane. NEVER an eye-level photograph, NEVER a close-up character-portrait crop.

The prompt that follows says WHAT is being drawn — a whole composed scene, a bare walkable surface, a sheet of props, or a character. Follow it exactly, including what it says about the background: this paragraph fixes the camera and nothing else.
style: Detailed 16-bit pixel art matching this game's own established look (see reference/the-game/inspo-*.png and the character portraits already generated, e.g. michael.png, kat.png) — NOT Stardew Valley's flat cel-shading. Rich, saturated color with real depth: warm light sources (lanterns, windows, candles) casting an actual warm glow against cooler ambient walls/shadow, visible texture on surfaces (brick coursing, wood grain, fabric folds), confident dark outlines. Still requires clean, sharply readable orthogonal architecture — walls meet the floor at a clear line, furniture silhouettes are unambiguous — richness of color/lighting must never come at the cost of the room reading as a coherent walkable space. For a CHARACTER SPRITE: same rich rendering technique and palette as the portrait busts, at a small full-body top-down scale, head-to-feet, clean readable silhouette from the overhead angle.
palette: Saturated, warm-vs-cool contrast — warm amber/gold light pooling against cooler blue, indigo, or wood-brown ambient tone, matching the inspiration images (e.g. inspo-08's warm doorway/window glow against cool blue brick walls). Not evenly lit throughout — real light sources create real pools of brighter warm light against a moodier surrounding tone, as long as the overall room still reads clearly (no area so dark the architecture becomes ambiguous).
background: For a PROP SHEET or a SPRITE SHEET: every item isolated on FLAT PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF), uniform, hard-edged, with a wide white band between items and a generous white margin — never transparency, which comes back as a beige wash. For a single CHARACTER SPRITE: isolated on a transparent background, no scene/ground/shadow drawn in. For anything else, the prompt says.
constraints: No text, no logos, no watermark, no UI elements, no borders/frames or vignette baked into the image. STRICTLY no people, characters or figures anywhere in a room or on a prop sheet — a stray figure standing in the scene is a confirmed failure mode. Architecture must be clean and orthogonal — walls meet the floor at a clear, readable line — and rich atmospheric lighting/colour is expected and desired, not a flaw. A character sprite must be full body head-to-feet, standing, facing the viewer — never a close-up bust crop — and isolated ONLY on plain transparent background with no scene, room, walls, furniture or floor drawn in. Any character wearing glasses must have clearly visible human eyes — pupils and eye whites — showing behind the lenses, never blank/hidden skin tone.
